9: // startsWithEvaluation checks if the given property starts with a certain prefix.
10: // It returns 'true', if the value of the given property starts with the prefix, 'false' if not.
11: // As an example, it can be used in the following way inside an 'if' evaluation:

20: //	}
21: //
22: // This rule can be applied to the following data object, where the evaluation will resolve to 'true':
23: //
24: // { "email": "user@faas.com" }
25: //
26: // Note that the 'starts_with'  evaluation rule must contain exactly two items, which both resolve to a

32: 		return nil
33: 	}
34: 	return strings.HasPrefix(propertyValue, target)
35: }

65: // parseStringComparisonEvaluationData tries to parse the input for the starts_with/ends_with evaluation.
66: // this evaluator requires an array containing exactly two strings.
67: // Note that, when used with jsonLogic, those two items can also have been objects in the original 'values' object,
68: // which have been resolved to string values by jsonLogic before this function is called.
69: // As an example, the following values object:
70: //
71: //	{
72: //	  "if": [
73: //			{
74: //				"starts_with": [{"var": "email"}, "user@faas"]
75: //			},
76: //			"red", null
77: //			]
78: //	}
79: //
80: // with the following data object:
81: //
82: // { "email": "user@faas.com" }
83: //
84: // will have been resolved to
85: //
86: // ["user@faas.com", "user@faas"]
87: //
88: // at the time this function is reached.
89: func parseStringComparisonEvaluationData(values interface{}) (string, string, error) {
90: 	parsed, ok := values.([]interface{})
91: 	if !ok {
92: 		return "", "", errors.New("[start/end]s_with evaluation is not an array")
93: 	}
94: 
95: 	if len(parsed) != 2 {
96: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation must contain a value and a comparison target")
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	property, ok := parsed[0].(string)
100: 	if !ok {
101: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation: property did not resolve to a string value")
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	targetValue, ok := parsed[1].(string)
105: 	if !ok {
106: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation: target value did not resolve to a string value")
107: 	}
108: 
109: 	return property, targetValue, nil
